findings.title: Design-batch resumes reject already-created designs
findings.description: A `slices-plan` item whose design was created but whose review exhausted its rounds is no longer returned by `cf.undesigned_slices`. Both retry and accept therefore reject the flagged item instead of resolving it. Reproduced with an open slice having a design file. The planning-batch test hides this by returning no design whenever queried with the plan. Support recovery from the post-design state and test that realistic case.

findings.title: Validate worktree registration before restoring the target
findings.description: Unlike `enter_slice_branch`, this path never checks worktree registration before using cf’s integration target. In an unregistered linked worktree, that target belongs to the primary checkout. `restore_target` can commit leftovers and attempt checkout before the later branch action rejects the worktree; planning batches have no branch action to perform that check. Enforce registration before any mutation.

findings.title: Item-resume preparation blocks the event loop
findings.description: The async resume path directly performs state-file reads, synchronous git subprocesses, cf calls, and report writes. These cannot satisfy the required sub-millisecond synchronous-work bound and prevent other asyncio tasks from progressing during slow operations. Offload blocking preparation and persistence, with explicit ownership of mutable report state, and add an event-loop responsiveness test.

findings.title: Malformed report items escape schema-error handling
findings.description: `cast` does not validate the external JSON structure. A report containing `"items": [null]` raises `AttributeError` in `BatchItemRecord.from_json`, bypassing `BatchReportLoadError` and the resume command’s controlled rejection path. Reproduced directly. Validate the report and item shapes with Pydantic and test malformed nested values.
